title: Bernoulli trials and the binomial distribution
terms: Bernoulli trial; success probability; failure probability; binomial distribution; binomial probability mass function; binomial mode.

The probability of an even binomial count is P (X even) = [1 + (1 − 2p) ]/2, obtained by adding

cases p = 0 and p = 1, the binomial law is concentrated at zero and n, respectively.

question.text:
For X ∼ Bin(8, p) with 0 < p < 1, suppose P (X = 3) = P (X = 4). What is p?
(A) 1/3 (B) 2/5 (C) 4/9 (D) 1/2 (E) 5/9

solution.text:
The ratio is P (X = 4)/P (X = 3) = (5/4)p/(1−p). Setting it equal to one gives 5p = 4(1−p),
hence p = 4/9.

question.text:
Independent variables X, Y are Bernoulli with success probabilities p, q ∈ (0, 1), respectively. If
X + Y has a Bin(2, r) distribution, which condition is necessary?
(A) p + q = 1 (B) p = q = r (C) r = pq (D) r = p + q (E) p = 1 − q = r

solution.text:
2
Matching means gives p + q = 2r. Matching the probability of two successes gives pq = r .
2 2
Hence (p − q) = (p + q) − 4pq = 0, so p = q = r. Conversely, equal success probabilities and
independence do produce a binomial sum. Independence alone is insufficient.
